newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Full Federal Court's decision to throw out a scheme designed to prevent Super League from competing with the Australian Rugby League has thrown new life into competition laws that will enable the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission to overturn a greater number of anti-competitive arrangements. Page 1.

Speaking on the Ten Network's Meet the Press program yesterday, Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge stepped up pressure on the Australian Democrats and the Opposition to pass the Budget measure to stop around 500 medical students practising as GPs, warning Medicare would collapse if the number wasn't cut. Page 3.

After Federal Treasurer Peter Costello told a New York audience he doubted Australia was going to go it alone and have a Government-owned telephone company. Senator Brian Harradine raised doubts about his support for the sale, saying Costello's comments were unhelpful. Page 3.

New South Wales Premier Bob Carr yesterday unveiled a plan to pay for the tolls on the M4 and M5 motorways, while keeping the Federal tax benefits associated with the financing of the roads, casting doubts over the future of infrastructure bonds. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

According to leading lawyers, sporting organisations will face increased scrutiny under the Trade Practices Act from now on due to a decision by the Full Federal Court to grant Super League the right to organise its own rugby league games. Page 1.

Six men and four women aged in their early twenties collapsed outside B3, a Gold Coast dance club, early yesterday morning prompting police to issue a national warning about a potentially fatal new designer drug. A police spokesman said last night Fantasy, a relative of Ecstasy, had been preliminarily identified as the drug involved. Page 1.

A letter to Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone from Prime Minister John Howard, sent in July, expressed doubts about the practical and material benefits of the national inquiry into the stolen generation. Howard suggested funding would be better spent in areas such as health, housing, education and employment. Page 1.

The future of the Australian Rugby League was in the hands of television magnate Kerry Packer, who holds the free-to-air rights to ARL games and who persuaded the ARL clubs to reject the original approaches from Super League, and the subscription television provider Optus Vision, who has announced its continuing support for the ARL despite the Super League green light, as the prospect of immediate talks with Super League faded. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The New South Wales Government yesterday announced a "cash-back" programme, which will cost an estimated A$74 million a year, which will see western Sydney motorists reimbursed for using the M4 and M5 tollways. The average M5 user can expect cheques totallig about A$1,250 a year as a result of the programme. Page 1.

A summary of the International Monetary Fund's assessment of the Australian economy, completed after the Federal election, urges the Howard Government to cut unemployment benefits and workers' benefits such as sick leave in an effort to reduce unemployment, but the recommendations have been rejected by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello. Page 1.

After being branded a racist by New South Wales Labor Party general secretary John Della Bosca, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday accused the Federal Opposition of using "McCarthyist" tactics. Howard is under increasing pressure to publicly reject comments mde by Independent MP Pauline Hanson on immigration. Page 1.

Eight people, aged in their twenties, were fighting for their lives in the Gold Coast Hospital last night after overdosing on a drug, thought to be Fantasy, and collapsing at a Gold Coast nightclub yesterday morning. Page 3.
THE AGE

As many hospitals prepare to cut budgets and staff further in 1996-7, Professor Stephen Duckett, who was acute health services director early in the Kennett Government's first term and helped introduce case-mix in July 1993, yesterday criticised the goverment for cutting hospital funding too deeply too quickly. Page A1.

In the midst of the ongoing racism debate - sparked last month by the first parliamentary speech by Independent MP Pauline Hanson - Opposition Leader Kim Beazley said yesterday Prime Minister John Howard was "playing with fire" by not speaking out against racism and risked irreparably damaging Australian society. Page A1.

The State Public Services Federation yesterday challenged the Victorian Government to support the third A$8-a-week safety-net increase granted to all low-paid workers under Accord Mark 7, worth A$416 a year, following this week's two per cent rise in MPs' salaries. Page A3.

Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone said yesterday the Territory's two Federal MPs, Grant Tambling and Nick Dondas, could be forced to resign over the euthanasia debate if Liberal MP Kevin Andrews' Federal Bill to overturn the Northern Territorys controversial euthanasia law was successful. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
